label: Spinner probability representation comparison
adaptation_note: Separate partitions, enlarged hub pointers and ordered outcome-code views retain nine versus four equal-sector models. Outcome code orientation is standardized; category identity and multiplicity are unchanged.
acceptance_requirement: Preserve nine equal sectors with three repeated categories versus four equal sectors with distinct categories. Keep pointer/hub roles; do not substitute eight sectors for nine.

frames.title: 9-sector spinner partition
frames.teaching_key: 9 equal angular sectors around a central hub; start at the top boundary and count clockwise. The next frame shows the hub pointer enlarged, followed by one outcome code for each sector in that same order. Circle, triangle, square repeat three times: each category occupies three of nine sectors. Grid stair steps approximate the equal angles; use the stated model, not pin area, for probability.

frames.title: 9-sector spinner hub pointer
frames.teaching_key: Enlarged hub only for the 9-sector spinner. Pointer aims into the first sector immediately clockwise from top. This is an example pointer position, not a probability bias. Ring is the hub, not the outer spinner rim.

frames.title: 9-sector spinner: outcome 1, circle
frames.teaching_key: Outcome code in sector 1 of 9, counted clockwise from the top radial boundary: circle. This enlarged code belongs to that sector in the partition overview. It is not another spinner or a change of sector size.
